notes: Event date: USHMM and Wikipedia: the 4th Armored Division landed at Utah Beach on 11 July 1944. Event definition: the first landing of the division at Utah Beach. The 13 July row (preferred) is the CMH ETO-OB chronology date for arrival on the Continent, with the division command post at Mesnil-St-Martin on that date; the two may describe different phases (first elements ashore, main body ashore, command post established) rather than a disagreement. A reviewer said the 704th Tank Destroyer Battalion boarded 11 July and landed 12 July; that was not confirmed (tankdestroyer.net, citing Yeide, has the battalion landing on 13 July). Location: Utah Beach area (OpenStreetMap Nominatim); the Mesnil-St-Martin command post this row reused belongs to the 13 July row only.

location_name: vicinity of Mesnil-St-Martin, Manche (unresolved CMH place name)
notes: Event date: CMH ETO-OB chronology: arrived on the Continent 13 July 1944. Event definition: arrival of the division on the Continent as CMH records it, with the command post at the vicinity of Mesnil-St-Martin, Manche, listed on this date (CMH gives the CP only as a vicinity of the town). Wikipedia and USHMM give 11 July for the Utah Beach landing (alternate row): the rows may describe different phases of the landing. Location caveat: the CMH CP name "Mesnil-St-Martin" could not be resolved to a Manche commune with certainty. The Nominatim match used before (about 49.0, -1.29, near Percy) lies roughly 50 km from the landing beaches and is inconsistent with the later CP at Méautis (17-18 July) and with a unit that had just landed at Utah Beach (Coutances was not taken until 28 July); the point is therefore unreliable and is kept only as a very wide inferred point. The unit was in the Cotentin beachhead assembly area (a 37th Tank Battalion report puts the division assembly area in use on 12 July).

notes: Event date: 22 December 1944 (Ardennes p524: at 0600 on 22 December, H-hour for the III Corps counterattack, two combat commands stood ready behind a line of departure from Habay-la-Neuve east to Niedercolpach; General Gaffey planned to attack with CCA and CCB abreast along the Arlon-Bastogne road; p509: D-day for the counterattack was 22 December). Event definition: III Corps' armored spearhead starts the relief of Bastogne from the south; the division makes slow progress through 25 December, and the link-up is the 26 December row. current_activity: relief column breaks through at Assenois at 1650 and contacts the Bastogne garrison
notes: Event date: 26 December 1944 (Ardennes p552: the plan for the attack on 26 December; p554: "At 1650 (the time is indelibly recorded in the 4th Armored Division record) Boggess saw some engineers in friendly uniform ... contact with the Bastogne garrison had been made"). Event definition: the division's relief of Bastogne. The spearhead was the Reserve Combat Command (CCR), commanded by Col. Wendell Blanchard, whose 37th Tank Battalion (Lt. Col. Creighton Abrams) and 53rd Armored Infantry Battalion dashed through Assenois and met the 326th Airborne Engineers of the 101st; the CCR component is recorded on its own row (C0566). The road stayed narrow and under fire for several days. An earlier version of this row called the CCR commander Abrams; he commanded the 37th Tank Battalion. Relationship: III Corps and Third Army (CMH table, from 19 December). Location: Assenois, the place the division's lead element captured, used as a representative point for the division, whose headquarters was not there (the division headquarters place on 26 December is not recorded in this row). Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Assenois, Vaux-sur-Sûre, Bastogne, Luxembourg, Wallonie, 6640, België / Belgique. Event support: high (a timed contact in the Green Book). Location support: moderate (the village is certain; it is the objective of the division's spearhead, not the division's own position). Objective check: the strategic objective was Bastogne; the contact is documented at Assenois on the row date, so Assenois is the place captured and Bastogne is not claimed.
